name: capget
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_capget, cap_user_header_t hdrp, cap_user_data_t datap);
description: The capget system call retrieves the capabilities of a specified thread. It uses a header structure to provide the capability version and PID, and stores the capability sets in a data structure. This interface is Linux-specific and may change across kernel versions.

parameters.name: hdrp
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing the capability version and PID of the thread.

parameters.name: datap
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure to hold the effective, permitted, and inheritable capability sets.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Bad memory address; hdrp must not be NULL, and datap may be NULL only when determining the preferred capability version.
One of the arguments was invalid.
An attempt was made to perform an operation without sufficient privileges.

bugs: In kernels before Linux 2.6.11, capset() could fail if a thread without the CAP_SETPCAP capability tried to change its own capabilities by specifying a nonzero PID.
versions: Linux-specific; structures introduced with versions like _LINUX_CAPABILITY_VERSION_1 in early kernels, up to _LINUX_CAPABILITY_VERSION_3 in Linux 2.6.26.
